main_text.p: 27 Itaq; quisquis ederit panem hunc, aut biberit poculum domini indignè, reus erit corporis & sanguinis domini.
28 Probet autem homo seipsum, & sic de pane edat, & de poculo bibat.
Tertiò, comminatione diuinæ iræ cui se obnoxios faciunt quicunque vllo modo has sacras res indignè tractant.
29 Nam edens & bibens indignè, iudicium sibi ipsi edit & bibit non diiudicans corpus domini.
30 Propter hoc multi inter vos imbecilles, & infirmi, & multi dormiunt.
31 Etenim si nos metipsos iudicaremus, non vtique iudicaremur.
32 Sed dum iudicamur, castigamur à domino, ne cum mundo condemnaremur. Vltimo in loco conclusio adjicitur, istius abusus reformationem habens.
33 Itaque fratres mei, quum convenitis ad edendum, aliy alios expectate.
34 Si autem quis esurit, domi edat, ut non ad judicium conveniatis: Reliqua autem, ut venero, ordinabo.

page.notes: Lower part of the page is cut off; the text ends mid-verse 32. Line 'inualidi' in verse 30 read as 'infirmi' is uncertain: printed text reads "inualidi". Copy as printed: "inualidi, & multi dormiunt." Some words in italic lines are only partly legible (e.g. "ne cum mundo condemnaremur" last line). Fragments of marginal text at the right edge are too cropped to read and are not transcribed. The catchword-like word "Verf." is printed at the right as a signature-like line and is transcribed as a paragraph.
